transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Reyes (Clipper - Head of ML), Maya Patel (Clipper - Platform Engineer), Ethan Zhou (Clipper - CTO)

Summary (auto): scoping POC for 4 weeks to validate capacity and autoscaling; collect traces and run benchmarks; deliver proposal for reserved GPU sizing and burst strategy.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood inference, i'm the account owner here. with me is priya, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Daniel: good thanks, yeah excited to get into this. short background — we're Clipper Analytics, building real-time document summarization and search features, heavy embedding + generation.
[00:14] Maya: hi all, maya here, i'm on infra, i'll be the one hooking up networking and traces.
[00:18] Ethan: hey everyone, ethan, ct o. main goal: validate cost & latency tradeoffs before a full prod rollout.
[00:24] Priya: great, quick agenda — confirm success criteria, share current workload numbers, discuss reserved capacity sizing and burst policy, fallback model options, telemetry for benchmarks, timeline. sound good?
[00:31] Daniel: yep that's perfect.

---
[00:36] Priya: to start, can you walk us through your expected qps and typical sequence lengths? and what models you want to test?
[00:42] Daniel: sure, baseline is about 30 rps for embeddings during business hours, peaks to 120 rps for generation across multiple endpoints. seq lengths vary: embeddings short (~64 tokens), generation average 300 tokens, occasionally up to 1k for long docs. preferred model family is an open LLM, similar to gpt-style, we're flexible on size — 7b to 13b.
[01:05] Alex: ok great, that helps. for the poc we recommend testing one gen model and embeddings model. success criteria — what are you targeting? latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy?
[01:14] Ethan: primary is 95th latency under 600ms for short completions (<=300 tokens) and cost below our current baseline which is about $0.40 per 1k tokens (we'd like 20% cost improvement). reliability is second: <1% error rate.
[01:27] Daniel: also want to validate autoscaling when traffic spikes — we need burst up to 300 rps for embeddings for short periods (few hours).

---
[01:36] Priya: that's clear. on redwood side we can do a Dedicated reserved pool for the POC — e.g., reserved GPUs to hit steady-state, plus burst capacity that borrows from on-demand or hosted endpoints. Important tradeoffs: reserved capacity guarantees throughput and lower unit cost; burst covers spikes but may have slightly higher latency if it routes to a hosted instance.
[01:58] Maya: what's the typical cold-start impact when bursting to hosted? we care about tail latency.
[02:03] Priya: good q — for short lived bursts we route to compatible model variants on hosted infra. the extra network hop and instance warmup can add ~150-300ms to 95th depending on model and sequence length; we mitigate with pre-warming and lightweight warm caches. also possible to reserve a small buffer of ephemeral GPUs for faster burst ramp.
[02:22] Alex: also note we have prefix caching/KV cache options which reduce work for repeated contexts and lower effective latency for sessions. but cache hit rate depends on your workload.

---
[02:31] Daniel: for the reserved side, how many gpus would you propose for our steady 30 rps generative throughput?
[02:36] Priya: depends on model selection and batch strategy. rough rule: a single A10G-equivalent for a 7b model with optimized kernels and batching can handle ~8-12 rps for 300-token gen at p95 ~300-450ms depending on batching. for embeddings, one GPU can handle several hundred small embedding requests due to batching efficiency. so for steady 30 rps gen we might propose 3 reserved GPUs (7b) to give headroom and autoscale buffer.
[03:04] Ethan: that seems conservative, but ok. for peaks to 120 rps we'd rely on burst — what's cost impact if burst is used frequently?
[03:11] Priya: burst to hosted is usage-based; we can model two scenarios: infrequent spikes (<=10% of time) will have small billing delta; frequent bursts we recommend increasing reserved commit or adding a scheduled autoscale window. We can run a cost model in the proposal.

---
[03:24] Maya: talking about autoscaling policies — do you support ramp-based scaling vs instant provisioning? how do you protect from runaway spend?
[03:30] Priya: we support policy types: threshold-based scaling, predictive scheduled scaling, and a burst cap with budget limits. we also allow fallback policies to route to cheaper quantized variants or earlier model versions if budget threshold hit. runaway spend protections: cap on max replicas, per-hour spend caps with alerting, and automatic degrade-to-cheaper-model policy.
[03:49] Daniel: can fallback policy maintain latency? if we route to a quantized 4-bit variant, we might see lower quality. need to define acceptance criteria per route.
[03:57] Alex: agreed — part of POC success criteria is to include quality checks. we'll run automated evals on sample prompts to measure quality delta for quantized/fallback variants; if quality falls below agreed threshold then fallback is only for non-critical routes.

---
[04:12] Priya: on benchmarking, we'll need: model config, batch sizes, sequence length distribution, concurrency targets, and a request trace. maya, would you be able to upload a week's trace or synthetic generator?
[04:21] Maya: yes we'll provide a one-week production trace with masked PII, should be able to get that by next thursday.
[04:26] Priya: perfect. telemetry we'll collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU util, batch sizes, cache hit rate, error rates, and cost per token. we'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet and a dashboard link.

---
[04:40] Ethan: timeline — we want results before end of march. does a 4-week POC fit that?
[04:44] Alex: yes. timeline proposal: week 1 (setup & access, upload traces, baseline runs), weeks 2-3 (live benchmarks + tuning), week 4 (reporting & decision). if we start mid-feb that fits.
[04:55] Daniel: sounds good. any enterprise compliance needs? we will need SOC2 and audit logs for the dedicated setup.
[05:01] Alex: we have SOC2 and can share security docs; Dedicated supports customer KMS/HSM for key management and VPC peering. we'll attach the security pack to the follow-up.

---
[05:12] Maya: network-wise we prefer VPC peering; do you support private endpoints and no egress to public internet?
[05:17] Priya: yes, Dedicated + Private supports VPC peering and air-gapped options. for POC we can provision a private control plane with limited egress. we'll include the network design doc.

---
[05:27] Daniel: on metrics for success — let's define explicit success criteria now:
[05:30] Daniel (cont): 1) p95 latency <= 600ms for <=300-token gen for 95% of requests; 2) cost reduction >= 20% vs current baseline for comparable throughput; 3) autoscale handles 300 rps embedding bursts with <2% error rate and p95 under 800ms when bursting; and 4) quality delta for fallback variant <= 3% on our eval metric.
[05:47] Priya: that's comprehensive, we'll include those as the POC success criteria in the proposal.

---
[05:52] Alex: ok next — pricing/practicals: reserved commit for 3 GPUs for the duration plus burst on-demand. we can do monthly pro-rata for a 4-week POC. i'll draft numbers and include alternatives: 2 reserved + higher burst vs 4 reserved + no burst depending on cost tolerance.
[06:07] Ethan: please include a sensitivity table showing cost if burst used 5%, 15%, 30% of time.
[06:13] Alex: noted.

---
[06:17] Maya: on observability — will we get token-level cost & latency breakdown and per-route dashboards?
[06:22] Priya: yes — console provides per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and exportable CSVs. for the POC we'll provide a dashboard with the collected metrics and a link to the benchmark sheet.

---
[06:30] Daniel: any gotchas we should be aware of? model warmup, kv cache effectiveness, and quantization compatibility?
[06:36] Priya: kv cache helps for repeated context, but for single-shot requests it doesn't help as much. quantization works for many open models; we test accuracy regressions as part of model onboarding. also note that batching tradeoffs: larger batches are cheaper but can increase latency; we'll tune batching thresholds for your latency SLOs.

---
[06:49] Ethan: ok, let's recap.
[06:51] Alex: recap — Redwood to send: 1) POC proposal with reserved GPU sizing, burst strategy, fallback policies, and pricing (alex); 2) benchmark config and metrics plan (priya); 3) security & network docs (alex/priya); Clipper to send: 1) one-week request trace and target SLOs (maya), 2) confirm internal stakeholders and schedule for benchmark week. live benchmark tentatively week of 2025-02-17.
[07:14] Daniel: agreed. one more Q — if we see quality issues on quantized fallback, can we force route to a higher-quality hosted model even if cost goes up?
[07:22] Priya: yes, there are policies to prefer quality over cost for specific routes. we can set route-level policies. we'll document examples in the proposal.

---
[07:30] Maya: thanks, this is helpful. expect the traces by 2025-02-13.
[07:34] Alex: perfect. we'll follow up with the proposal by 2025-02-14 and set up the benchmark run. thanks everyone.
[07:40] Ethan: thanks all.
